title: Pull Requests
subtitle: Propose, review, and merge changes on GitHub
author: KERNAL Team

whyItExists.problem: On a shared codebase, anyone pushing directly to main can break things for everyone. You need a process to propose, review, and approve changes before they land.
whyItExists.solution: A Pull Request is a proposal to merge one branch into another. It shows the diff, collects reviewer comments, runs CI checks, and records the decision — all before any merge happens.
whyItExists.whenToUse: For any change to a shared branch. Even solo projects benefit: PRs force you to review your own changes before merging.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: Tiny solo projects where you're the only contributor can skip PRs. But on any team project, PRs are non-negotiable.

explainModes.beginner: A Pull Request is how you say 'I'd like to add these changes to the main codebase. Can someone review it first?' Reviewers look at the diff, leave comments, and approve or request changes. Once approved, it gets merged.
explainModes.simple: Create a branch → push it → click 'Compare & pull request' on GitHub → fill in description → assign reviewers → wait for review → address comments → approved → merge. The PR shows exactly which commits and lines changed.
explainModes.standard: A PR has: title, description, commits, diff (Files changed tab), reviewers, labels, milestone, linked issues. Review states: Comment (feedback only), Approve, Request changes. Required reviews and status checks can block merging. Merge strategies: merge commit, squash and merge, rebase and merge.
explainModes.technical: GitHub's PR system uses refs: refs/pull/<number>/head (the PR branch) and refs/pull/<number>/merge (the merge preview). Draft PRs signal WIP. CODEOWNERS file routes reviews to the right team. Protected branches enforce rules: minimum approvals, dismiss stale reviews, require status checks. GitHub Actions can auto-label PRs, run linters, post coverage reports as PR comments.
explainModes.deepDive: GitHub's review system creates review threads per diff hunk. Suggestion blocks (```suggestion) let reviewers propose exact code changes the author can apply with one click. Co-authored commits (Co-authored-by:) give credit to pair reviewers. Auto-merge (git merge when all checks pass) speeds up high-trust workflows. Merge queues (GitHub Enterprise) serialize concurrent PRs to prevent integration failures.

content.code:
# 1. Create and push a feature branch
git switch -c feature/user-profile
# ... make changes ...
git add .
git commit -m "Add user profile page"
git push -u origin feature/user-profile

# GitHub shows a banner: 'Compare & pull request'
# Click it, or use the GitHub CLI:

gh pr create \
  --title "Add user profile page" \
  --body "Closes #42. Adds profile page with avatar, bio, and stats." \
  --reviewer teammate-username

# See your open PRs
gh pr list

# Check out a teammate's PR locally to test it
gh pr checkout 42

## What changed
- Added `/profile` route with UserProfile component
- Avatar upload using existing S3 integration
- Bio field limited to 160 characters (Twitter-style)

## Why
Closes #42 — users requested the ability to customise their public profile.

## How to test
1. Log in, click your avatar → 'Edit profile'
2. Upload a photo — check it appears in the header
3. Edit bio, save — confirm it persists on reload

## Screenshots
[Attach before/after screenshots here]

## Checklist
- [x] Tests added
- [x] Mobile-responsive
- [x] Accessibility: form labels, ARIA

# Check out the PR locally
gh pr checkout 42

# Run it, test it
npm run dev

# Leave a review via CLI
gh pr review 42 --approve --body "Looks great! Tested locally."
gh pr review 42 --request-changes --body "Please add error handling for network failure"

# After approval — merge
gh pr merge 42 --squash --delete-branch
# Options: --merge (merge commit), --squash (one commit), --rebase

questions.question: What is the purpose of a Pull Request?
options: To pull changes from a remote
To propose merging a branch, show the diff, and enable code review before merging
To delete a branch from GitHub
questions.explanation: A PR proposes merging one branch into another. It shows the diff, allows comments and reviews, runs CI checks, and records who approved it — all before the merge happens. The name 'pull request' means 'please pull my changes into your branch'.

faq.q: Should I squash, merge, or rebase merge a PR?
faq.a: Squash (all PR commits → one commit on main) — clean history, best for most PRs. Merge commit (preserves all commits + adds a merge commit) — useful when branch history matters. Rebase and merge (replays each commit onto main linearly, no merge commit) — clean but rewrites hashes. Most teams pick one strategy and stick to it.

faq.q: What does 'Closes #42' in a PR description do?
faq.a: GitHub automatically links the PR to issue #42 and closes the issue when the PR is merged. Also works with: Fixes #42, Resolves #42.

examples: GitHub's own codebase has thousands of open PRs — all merged via PR, including by core engineers
Draft PRs ('WIP: ...') signal to teammates that review isn't needed yet
CODEOWNERS auto-assigns reviewers based on which files were changed
